stem.en: Kabir asks why the resting voltage "sits at minus seventy and not at zero, since the pump is only moving ions". Where does the voltage come from?

text.en: From potassium leaking out through its channels, carrying charge out, until the inside's negativity pulls back exactly as hard as the gradient pushes out. The pump built the gradient; the leak turns it into a voltage.

feedback.en: The pump's charge imbalance is small. Most of the voltage is the potassium leak balancing against its own gradient.
Sodium rushing in would make the inside positive. At rest sodium barely leaks. Its rush is tomorrow, and it is the message.

text.en: From the wall itself, which is charged.

feedback.en: A bilayer has no charge of its own. The charge is ions on either side.

explanation.en: A gradient plus a leak that passes only one ion gives a voltage. The voltage sits where the electrical pull equals the diffusion push.
